description:
Address a single gate-run record by its issue and its run id, so loading one run never needs to know where other issues' runs live.

## Background

`IssueStore::load_gate_run_result` (`crates/jit/src/storage/mod.rs:262`) takes a run id alone. The JSON backend implements it at `storage/json.rs:1395` and the memory backend at `storage/memory.rs:909`. The test-only callers are in `storage/gate_runs.rs`. Two integration-test wrappers implement the trait by forwarding: `tests/fast_docs_templates/template_apply_atomicity_tests.rs:157-168` and `tests/fast_rules/local_rule_enforcement_tests.rs:869-885`.

The executor's `get_gate_run_result` (`commands/gate.rs:1461-1463`) is the production caller. The server route `GET /issues/:id/gate-runs/:run_id` (`crates/server/src/routes.rs:909-920`) discards its `:id` segment and loads by run id alone.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `IssueStore::load_gate_run_result` takes `(&IssueId, &GateRunId)`. A record whose `issue_id` differs from the requested issue is reported as not found.
- [hard] REQ-02: The executor's `get_gate_run_result` takes the issue and the run id, and the server's single-run route passes its issue path segment.
- [hard] REQ-03: One storage conformance test, run against both backends, proves that loading a run under the wrong issue is not found and loading it under its own issue returns it.
- [hard] REQ-04: A server test shows that requesting a run under another issue's path returns 404.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: Gate-run records load by issue and run id
